paragraphs: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yaakov bar Giyori.

Hyman describes him as Rabbi Yohanan’s student, always sending teachings from the Land of Israel to Babylonia in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Eruvin 62a, Moed Katan 18a, Ketubot 46a and Chullin 101b. Taanit 29b has Rabbi Yitzchak bar Giyori speaking in Rabbi Yohanan’s name, with bar Yaakov missing in the middle.
Hyman explains Yuchasin’s statement that he lived in Rabbi’s time as a loss of abbreviation marks: he reconstructs רב״י, meaning Rabbi Yohanan.

notes.text: Hyman’s explanation is that abbreviation marks were lost, turning רב״י (Rabbi Yohanan) into רבי (Rabbi). The missing bar Yaakov and the correction are preserved as his claims.

Hyman’s “always” is preserved as his characterization of the transmissions. Eruvin 62a directly names Yitzchak bar Yaakov bar Giyori transmitting Rabbi Yochanan’s teaching. The Yuchasin printing-error account remains Hyman’s reconstruction.
